note: The symptom of this feature request is an ABSENCE: no HLSL spelling reaches the DXIL two-output ops IMul(41)/UMul(42)/UDiv(43), whose op class is named 'binaryWithTwoOuts' in dx.op function names (lib/DXIL/DxilOperations.cpp). A bare absence clause is worthless here for two documented reasons, so it carries three positive anchors. (a) 'define void @main()' cannot be emitted by a compile that failed, which blocks the 'absence predicate satisfied by a failed parse' trap. (b) 'udiv i32' and 'urem i32' assert the specific fallback the issue is about: quotient and remainder of ONE operand pair left as two independent LLVM instructions instead of one two-output UDiv. Anchoring on them also stops the predicate being vacuously true of any shader that simply never divides. If a future DXC fused the pair into dx.op.binaryWithTwoOuts, the udiv/urem anchors would disappear at the same moment the not_regex clause failed, so the predicate degrades to no-match in exactly the right direction. CONTROLS (all captured in this directory): variant-control-parse-error-main-debug.txt -- a shader with a deliberate syntax error, --expect no-match, proving a failed compile cannot satisfy the absence clause (it scores no-match, and its header records the E_FAIL exit). variant-control-no-divide-main-debug.txt -- a successfully compiling shader with no division, --expect no-match, proving the predicate does not fire on just any clean compile. variant-control-token-visible-main-debug.txt -- the repro compiled with -Zi -Qembed_debug so that the literal string dx.op.binaryWithTwoOuts, present in a source comment, is echoed into !dx.source.contents; --expect no-match, proving the not_regex clause really does fire when that text is present in the output rather than being unfalsifiable. The predicate CANNOT prove 'no HLSL construct anywhere reaches these ops' -- that claim rests on source inspection recorded in notes.md (no entry in utils/hct/gen_intrin_main.txt, and the only in-tree emitter is projects/dxilconv's DXBC converter).
